q6.answer: Each upload carries a change_id (UUID assigned when first queued, unchanged across retries). The server records every handled change_id in applied_changes with its stored result (accepted+version, or conflict+conflict note id). On a retry it finds the id, returns the stored result and applies nothing, all inside the same transaction that writes note, log and applied_changes.

q7.answer: In the phone's local SQLite sync_state table as a cursor, the highest log seq it has applied. It is updated in the same local transaction that applies a download page's entries, so the cursor and the applied notes move together.

q8.answer: Nothing from the partial page was applied and the cursor did not move, because a page is applied atomically. The next sync asks for entries after the same cursor and gets them again. No entries are skipped or applied twice, and applying is also idempotent via the version check.

q9.answer: The upload response returns a conflict result with the conflict note id, so the phone knows its edit lost. It then deletes the outbox row. On the download, the log entry for the original note carries the server's winning full note, and since its version is higher than the local server_version the phone replaces its local copy. The conflict note N2 (with the loser's text) arrives in the same download. The UI message about saving a copy is an open item.

q10.answer: Only after the phone reads that change's result (accepted or conflict) in an upload response, whether new or a replayed stored result. Timeouts, crashes or lost responses leave the row in place for resending with the same change_id.

q11.answer: If the note has a pending outbox row, the phone does not overwrite the local text but still advances the cursor. The pending change keeps its original base_version, so the server reports a conflict at upload and the losing text becomes a conflict note. I did not specify separate handling for the in-flight case beyond that. In the conflict case the later download replaces the local note with the server's version.

q12.answer: The in-flight outbox row is left untouched, so a retry sends exactly what the server may have seen. The new text is saved only to the local notes table. After an accepted ack, the phone creates a new outbox row with a new change_id and base_version equal to the version returned in the ack. If the in-flight change instead comes back as conflict, the later edit is lost, since the download replaces it with the server's version. That case is left as an open item, with the option of queuing it as another change against the new server version.
